annotations: Desktop web at 1280 × 800 and up: side navigation on every page, content in a single column with evidence and stats in rows.
Keyboard first: every list supports J/K and arrow keys, Enter opens, Esc goes back; single-key shortcuts only work while the list or panel has focus.
Exceptions is the home page. Exception opens as its own page so the URL can be shared with a reviewer.
Every automatic decision shown on screen names its rule; amounts show the original currency when it differs from the base currency.
Loading keeps headers and page titles in place; only the data area is replaced, and loading is announced.
assumptions: Most screens are 1280 px wide or more; below 1024 px the evidence cards stack
The queue shows 25 rows per page with keyboard paging
openQuestions: Should the Exception page keep the queue visible in a narrow column on wide screens?
Should Matched default to rows matched within tolerance, since exact matches need less checking?
